source_title: Victor — An AI Coworker That Lives in Slack
speaker: Frederick Vichowski (Co-founder of Victor, formerly JACE)
key_insight: Company agents (not personal agents) are the employee metaphor made real — one admin connects integrations for the whole team, Slack hides 10-minute agent latency, and memory/permissions/tone must be re-architected because they don't scale linearly from the personal-agent case.

discovered_urls.context: Victor product — Slack-native AI coworker with 3,000+ Pipedream integrations, launched Feb 2026, immediate PMF. Relevant for understanding scoping feature + team permission model.
JACE — Vichowski's 2024 email agent built in Sonnet 3.5 era. Still operational. Historical reference for the persistent-context + proactivity pattern that evolved into Victor.
Pipedream — the 3,000+ integration connector layer Victor builds on. Reference for any future integration-breadth evaluation in our own orchestrator work.

Web Arena benchmark — JCAI (Vichowski's 2023 product) achieved state-of-the-art here using lossless DOM minification. Useful historical context for browser-agent reliability ceiling (60%/step compounds to ~8%).
Full AIE Europe 2026 London session recording — Vichowski's talk starts at t=22426s (~6h13m). Other talks in the same stream already ingested (Ubl, Steinberger, Hadsell, Lopopolo, Radik, Vincent).

cross_references.relation: Same AIE Europe 2026 day — both talks identify memory and permissions at scale as core agent-security problems. Victor explicitly references OpenClaw memory clutter as the canonical failure mode they had to solve before launch.

action_items_for_our_orchestrator: Adopt 'personal integrations stay private to their owner' as a hard permission invariant for any future team-scoped agent
Apply latency-hiding principle to long-running tmux workers — route completion through an async channel (devlog, Slack, email), not a blocking web UI
Treat proactivity as an earned-trust gradient — default-off for new installs, opt-in expansion to power users first
Model agent tone as a product surface, not a debug toggle — validate personality before exposing agents to non-technical users
Plan for multi-channel context flattening (threads + DMs + reactions + edits + deletes) before any Slack integration
Add Pipedream to tool catalogue as the reference integration-connector layer
Add Vichowski's 'memory clutters N× faster at N users' finding as a cross-reference in the OpenClaw catalogue entry
